gaps.sentence: No sooner ___ the contract been signed than the rumours started.
gaps.explanation: 'No sooner had … been signed than …' — past perfect with inversion.

gaps.sentence: Not once ___ she mentioned the incident to anyone.
gaps.explanation: 'Not once has she mentioned' — inversion with the perfect.

gaps.sentence: Only when the last vote had been counted ___ the returning officer speak.
gaps.explanation: 'Only when' at the front forces question order: did the returning officer speak.

gaps.sentence: So convincing ___ her argument that even the sceptics agreed.
gaps.explanation: 'So convincing was her argument that …' — 'so + adj' fronted with inversion.

gaps.sentence: ___ you stands the man responsible for the discovery.
gaps.explanation: Dramatic inversion: 'Before you stands the man…' — the phrase of place is fronted and the verb precedes the subject.

gaps.sentence: Little ___ the villagers suspect that the mine would ever reopen.
gaps.explanation: 'Little did the villagers suspect' — they had no idea.

gaps.sentence: Rarely ___ this metro line run this late.
gaps.explanation: Rarely at the front: does + subject + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: Only later ___ it occur to her that the letter had been a forgery.
gaps.explanation: 'Only later' at the front inverts with do-support: did it occur to her.
